extracted.intended_audience: number theorists / arithmetic geometers and researchers evaluating Mochizuki's IUTT and the Scholze–Stix critique
extracted.subtask_description: A focused technical analysis of the mathematical completeness and deficiencies in Mochizuki's Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUTT) and of the Scholze–Stix critique; examines what precise inputs, constructions, and existence claims are required for a complete proof of the abc-conjecture in this framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative definition of Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s quantification of what it means to be an Arithmetic Holomorphic Structure is mathematically inadequate to quantitatively assert that one has two or more such structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete proof must give a precise, quantitative definition of 'Arithmetic Holomorphic Structure' that permits unambiguous demonstration of the existence of multiple distinct such structures; this is required because the proof of abc compares and averages arithmetic quantities arising from many such structures (needed for Mochizuki 2021c, Theorem 3.11 and Corollary 3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit exhibition of many distinct Arithmetic Holomorphic Structures
rubrics_metrics.description: One must explicitly exhibit the existence of many such structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete constructions (e.g. arising from rigid analytic spaces / p-adic holomorphic functions) showing multiple inequivalent structures so that averaging/comparison arguments are well-founded; mere assertion of existence is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include arbitrary algebraically closed perfectoid fields as geometric base-points
rubrics_metrics.description: Arbitrary algebraically closed perfectoid fields (one for every prime p) are included in the data of an arithmeticoid and serve as arbitrary geometric base-points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theory must allow arbitrary alg. closed perfectoid fields as input data for geometric base-points; these supply the (only) source of arbitrary geometric base-points for tempered fundamental groups required by Mochizuki's Key Principle of Inter-Universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly provide required input data (do not omit inputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no mention of the required input data in [Mochizuki, 2021a,b,c,d]; proofs must explicitly state required input data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid theory or proof must explicitly identify and include all required input data (e.g. geometric base-points, untilts, valuation data); omission of such data renders arguments incomplete or invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not restrict to \u00ef\u0192Q_p (Qbar_p) when arbitrary geometric base-points are required
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot build a valid theory by requiring arbitrary geometric base-points for tempered fundamental groups but work solely over Qbar_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If arbitrary geometric base-points are essential for constructions, the framework must work beyond Qbar_p; restricting to Qbar_p while assuming arbitrary geometric base-points is logically inconsistent and mathematically insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use valuation data (instead of relying only on Frobenioids)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with valuation data instead of Frobenioids for relevant constructions and computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuation data can serve directly for computing local and global arithmetic degrees and can replace or complement the use of Frobenioids; specify how valuation data enter the definitions and constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with the Frobenius morphism (log-Link) rather than a proxy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Frobenius morphism itself instead of a proxy (log-Link proxy arguments are inadequate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct and use a genuine global Frobenius (log-Link) where needed; avoid substituting proxies whose existence/nontriviality is not established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and non-triviality of log-Links (global Frobenius)
rubrics_metrics.description: log-Link = global Frobenius and it must be constructed and shown to be non-trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate construction and non-triviality of log-Links (global Frobenius); arguments that declare log-Links irrelevant or trivial without construction are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and role of Theta-Links
rubrics_metrics.description: Theta-Links (central in Mochizuki's theory and claimed via theory of Frobenioids) must be established and their role clarified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructions or replacements for Theta-Links where Mochizuki asserted them without clear establishment; show how they function in the framework (e.g. in canonical splittings of the log-theta lattice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for arbitrary geometric base-points as proxy for deformations
rubrics_metrics.description: Central role of arbitrary geometric base-points as a proxy for deformations of arithmetic (Mochizuki, 2021a, § I3, Page 25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat geometric base-points as part of the domain/codomain of key operations; show how they encode deformations and how key operations depend on distinct geometric base-points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove existence of distinct Hodge-Theaters, �Etale Pictures, and Frobenius Pictures
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrary to Scholze–Stix's assertion that such objects do not exist, a complete theory must demonstrate existence of distinct (1) Hodge-Theaters, (2) �etale Pictures, (3) Frobenius Pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructions and theorems establishing distinct Hodge-Theaters, distinct �etale Pictures, and distinct Frobenius Pictures (references given in the report to explicit propositions/theorems in Joshi's work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of isomorphs and arithmetic holomorphic structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of isomorphs and arithmetic holomorphic structures must be proved rather than asserted to be impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show existence theorems (e.g. isomorphs, labeled isomorphs, untilts of fundamental groups) and definitions of arithmetic holomorphic structures with proofs; arguments claiming impossibility must address these constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-triviality of the gau-Link including j^2-scaling and Galois action
rubrics_metrics.description: The gau-Link (Θgau-Link) can be non-trivial: it comes with a non-trivial j^2-scaling factor for j = 1,...,ℓ-1/2 and is equipped with a non-trivial Galois action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any critique asserting triviality must account for possible scaling factors and Galois actions; proofs should explicitly compute or display these structures and their non-triviality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of distinct prime-strips
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct prime-strips exist and must be established (they are used in some parts of the theory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructions and theorems showing distinct prime-strips and explain their role in the global theory (references to Joshi's results are cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a canonical formulation / Rosetta Stone mapping between theories
rubrics_metrics.description: A canonical formulation of the theory (a 'Rosetta Stone') is required; without it Mochizuki's work stands incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a canonical, transparent formulation that maps Mochizuki's objects to alternate constructions (e.g. Joshi's formulations), enabling parallel reading and comparison; this includes making precise how Mochizuki's Key Principle of Inter-Universality is implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate deformation properties of a fixed number field and Frobenius on deformation space
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that a fixed number field is topologically deformable and that there is a topological space of deformations with a Frobenius morphism on this space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the deformation space, exhibit the Frobenius morphism, and explain how these enable arithmetic-dynamical approaches in Diophantine geometry and feed into arguments like those for the abc-conjecture.
